title: OTLP multiplexer + tenant quota fence and histogram smoothing for inference KPIs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Inference traffic bursts and client-side misconfigurations create short-lived metric storms that (1) overload our Prometheus remote_write pipeline, (2) break histogram quantiles for per-model latency KPIs, and (3) make tenant-level cost attribution noisy. Current adapters either drop data wholesale or accept everything, causing downstream queueing and alert noise.

Goal: Build an OTLP multiplexer (sidecar/gateway) that accepts both OTLP and Prometheus remote_write inputs, performs tenant-aware quota fencing and adaptive throttling on bursts, and applies histogram smoothing and outlier dampening for inference-specific latency histograms before forwarding to our OTLP collector and Prometheus-native rollup service. The component should also attach trace hooks (trace_id/span_id) or correlators when present to enable causal attribution.

High-level approach:
- Insert a lightweight multiplexer as an ingest gateway in front of metric collectors for host/dedicated/vpc deployments.
- Implement tenant quota fence: token bucket per-tenant combined with short-term burst window and a graceful 429-style signalling to SDKs via well-documented headers or OTLP status codes.
- Adaptive throttling: detect surge patterns (per-tenant and per-route) and apply probabilistic sampling for high-cardinality series instead of deterministic drop.
- Histogram smoothing: apply an exponential smoothing kernel to latency histogram buckets and synthesize stable quantile anchors to prevent quantile oscillation from microbursts. Preserve TTL for raw samples (send downsampled smoothing + occasional raw snapshots).
- Trace enrichment: when OTLP traces or correlators present, attach trace identifiers to metric envelopes to enable trace->metric linking in the downstream correlation service.

Non-goals: full replacement of long-term rollup pipeline, persistent storage of raw per-request metrics beyond short retention window, and changing customer billing semantics in this iteration.
acceptance_criteria: Gateway accepts OTLP/gPRC and Prometheus remote_write and forwards to existing collector cluster with <5ms median added latency under steady-state load
Per-tenant token-bucket enforces configured quota with observable token usage metrics and emits quota_exceeded events to the audit log
Burst detection triggers probabilistic sampling reducing write volume by 60%+ for synthetic surge scenarios while preserving 95th/99th latency quantiles within 5% of raw baseline
Histogram smoothing reduces quantile oscillation in unit tests and on canary traffic; canary shows stable P95/99 across 10 synthetic microbursts
Trace IDs are preserved and attached in metric envelopes when available; downstream correlation tests can link traces to metric spikes
Integration tests cover OTLP auth, Prometheus label-preservation, tenant isolation, and backpressure behavior under loss of downstream collector
Documentation and SDK guidance updated with header semantics and recommended retry/backoff patterns
tasks: Design multiplexer API and config schema (per-tenant quotas, burst window, sampling policy)
Prototype adaptive throttling algorithm (simulate with replay of production ingest traces)
Implement histogram smoothing module and unit tests using synthetic latency distributions
Add trace correlation propagation and end-to-end test harness
Load test with canary cluster and measure latency/cpu/memory characteristics
Create rollout plan: staged canary (5%, 20%, 100%) with rollback hooks and alerting
Write operational runbook and update console telemetry dashboards for quota metrics
comments: 2025-02-16: Kickoff meeting notes — agreed to keep component lightweight (Go), reuse existing OTLP proto definitions, and prefer gRPC for OTLP path. Action: Aisha to draft schema, Marco to run initial replay tests.

2025-02-20: Spike results — prototype reduced influx from synthetic tenant storm by 72% using probabilistic sampling plus token-bucket. Memory overhead measured ~60MB per gateway instance under heavy load.

2025-02-24 (PM feedback): PM requests explicit metrics for 'tokens_used', 'tokens_dropped', 'smoothing_applied' and a customer-facing metric 'quota_signals' for billing/alerts. Also asked to avoid changing billing semantics in this rollout.
2025-02-27 (Design review): Design OK from telemetry team; noted concern about smoothing masking real regressions — agreed to emit raw_snapshot every 5 minutes as control signal.

2025-03-01 (Engineering update): Implemented OTLP multiplexer core and histogram smoother. End-to-end tests passing locally. Next: add tenant config API and integrate with tenancy service for quota values.
2025-03-02 (Security review stub): Submitted design doc to security for KMS/ACL review. Security suggested adding mutual TLS for dedicated/private deployments; marked as action item.
